text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Thursday:
- Helmuth Maucher, CEO of Swiss food giant Nestle, said he expects a net profit of more than three billion Swiss francs for fiscal 1996.

- Swiss government said it will not lower the budget for humanitarian help despite a huge deficit. However, insiders believe the allocated 1,050 million Swiss francs must last for a longer period than the budgeted four years.

- European Union Commissioner for Transport Neil Kinnock is putting pressure on E.U. transport ministers to support a bilateral agreement with Switzerland. Austria in particular is against such an agreement. Kinnock on Wednesday went to Vienna to discuss the issue.

- Scientists at the university of Berne started to investigate the role Swiss churches played during World War II. They are particulary interested in church attitude towards Jews and immigration policy during that period.
- Swiss engineering group Sulzer will axe 120 jobs at its locomotive making unit SLM.

- Troubled Swiss steel group Von Moos appointed Robert Jeker, a former head of bank Credit Suisse, as its new board chairman. In March, the group will decide on whether to close a steel manufacturing plant in Gerlafingen, ending hundreds of jobs.
